A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VTC-Bench research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison; v3 retains Appendices A–F and adds Appendix G.

before.justification: v2 reports original compression experiments on Qwen2-VL-7B and LLaVA-OV-7B, including accuracy comparisons, sample visualizations, and image-property analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical evaluations and additionally reports inference timings for downsampling and DART in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same inference, grouping, and aggregation procedure: exclude samples incorrectly answered by original Qwen2-VL, identify downsampling failures, and evaluate compression methods on that difficult subset.

E1.justification: Both versions use GQA, MMBench English and Chinese, MME, POPE, MMStar, OCRBench, and ChartQA. Appendix G measures runtime over the existing eight benchmarks without introducing new data or task conditions.

E2.justification: Table 6 removes the Downsample reference rows from the reported LLaVA-OV-7B group comparison at all five reduction ratios, retaining FastV, VisionZip, and PruMerge+. Other accuracy comparator sets remain unchanged; the new timing comparison uses existing methods, DART and downsampling.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces elapsed inference time across all eight benchmarks as an additional evaluation metric, comparing DART and downsampling using the same repository on one A800. Existing accuracy protocols and compression ratios are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds an analysis of whether progressively smaller token budgets yield corresponding runtime savings, finding limited runtime sensitivity for DART. The existing group-separation analyses, visual case studies, and image-property analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results come from a single run in Appendix A and report the same image-property means and standard deviations in Table 7. v3 adds no repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, or uncertainty analysis for its timings.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports timings, including 17,452 seconds for downsampling versus 25,200 for DART at 25% retained tokens. Table 6 loses its 0.0/100.0 Downsample entries. Appendix F changes the stated MMStar brightness range from 165–168 to 163–168; retained accuracy values and Table 7 statistics are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 1's relationship between downsampling and token compression, along with the operational group definitions, is unchanged. Neither version supplies formal proofs establishing the filtering mechanism's validity, and v3 adds no theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about benchmark task mismatch, downsampling as a difficulty discriminator, and VTC-Bench as an additional evaluation framework. The timing evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly attributes DART's limited runtime improvement, tentatively, to overhead from additional metric calculations and interprets the timings as supporting downsampling's efficiency. This mechanism is not directly isolated. The existing limitations in Section 6 remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly explains that timings are rough measurements obtained from logged inference start and end times across all eight benchmarks. Hardware, repositories, software versions, interpolation, compression controls, and code/data access statements otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds compression surveys by Yao, Shao, and Wu and newer MLLM/embodied-AI citations. It removes EmbodiedEval, EfficientVLA, and Wen et al.'s 'Token pruning in multimodal large language models: Are we solving the right problem?' Positioning relative to VisionThink and EffiVLM-Bench remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording, punctuation, capitalization, and bibliographic edits; updates affiliations and corresponding-author notation; and adds acknowledgments and Appendix G. The existing section order and most prose are preserved.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 8 and removes five reference rows from Table 6. It also changes table spacing, figure sizing, and page flow, notably enlarging Figure 2 and reducing Figure 5's displayed size. The existing figure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix G adds useful evidence about actual runtime, which v2 did not report, with a stated measurement procedure and shared code and hardware. Small corrections also improve consistency. The gain is limited because timings are rough, single-run comparisons involving only DART and downsampling, and the proposed overhead explanation remains untested; the framework's existing validity limitations persist.
